\chapter{A Message for Mira}
\label{ch:mr-a1-named-reader-message}
\hlchaptermodality{20}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can independently write a 32-word Devanagari message to Mira for a familiar introduction and Marathi-study purpose.}

Without romanization, a line bank, or a visible answer model, write the 30-40-word message from the named reader and purpose alone.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[namaskār Mīrā]{Write to one named reader}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M01-reader-greeting}



\begin{quote}
You already know \textbf{\mr{नमस्कार}}. A message needs to show who receives that greeting. Today the reader is \textbf{\mr{मीरा}}, the familiar practice name.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — observe and trace one complete line}
Trace \textbf{\mr{नमस्कार} \mr{मीरा}.} once. Leave one space between the greeting and the name. Touch the full stop; it closes this first line.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after one reader, one greeting, and one boundary.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mājhaṁ nāv Aruṇ āhe]{Add the sender's name}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M02-name-line}



\begin{quote}
Write yesterday's reader greeting from memory. The next line is not new Marathi: \textbf{\mr{माझं} \mr{नाव} \mr{अरुण} \mr{आहे}.} already appeared in the introduction recap.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — guided copy}
Copy the name line once beneath the greeting. Check only two things: \textbf{\mr{अरुण}} is the sender, and \textbf{\mr{आहे}} remains at the end before the full stop.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Two lines are enough for today.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bheṭūn ānand jhālā]{One line for meeting the reader}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M03-meeting-line}



\begin{quote}
Read the known line \textbf{\mr{भेटून} \mr{आनंद} \mr{झाला}.} Say where it ends. The full stop keeps the sender's name and the meeting response from running together.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — guided copy}
Copy \textbf{\mr{भेटून} \mr{आनंद} \mr{झाला}.} beneath the identity line. Compare the boundary first; compare spelling only after the full stop is present.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The opening now has three short lines; do not combine them yet.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[malā marāṭhī yete]{Begin the purpose: Marathi}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M04-language-line}



\begin{quote}
Say the known sentence \textbf{\mr{मला} \mr{मराठी} \mr{येते}.} Marathi puts the knower in the dative and lets \textbf{\mr{मराठी}} govern \textbf{\mr{येते}}. Nothing grammatical is being added.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — delayed copy}
Study \textbf{\mr{मला} \mr{मराठी} \mr{येते}.} for five seconds. Cover it, wait five more seconds, then write it. Repair the ending \textbf{-\mr{ते}} before any other spelling.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Only one purpose line today.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mī marāṭhī vāchto]{Add one reading line}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M05-reading-line}



\begin{quote}
The sender is Arun, so retrieve the already-practised masculine sentence: \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{मराठी} \mr{वाचतो}.} Today you are placing it in a message, not learning a verb.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — delayed copy}
Look once, hide the model, wait five seconds, and write the line. Check \textbf{\mr{वाचतो}} first. Do not add the next skill on the same line.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
One skill, one sentence, one full stop.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mī mājhaṁ nāv lihito]{Add one writing line}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M06-writing-line}



\begin{quote}
Read the old sentence \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{माझं} \mr{नाव} \mr{लिहितो}.} The middle names the object; the last word carries Arun's masculine ending.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — delayed copy}
Study the line, hide it, and wait eight seconds. Write it from memory. Compare in two passes: first \textbf{\mr{माझं} \mr{नाव}}, then \textbf{\mr{लिहितो}}. Repair only one pass today.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The first three purpose lines now exist separately. Combining them comes later.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mī bolto]{Add the shortest skill line}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M07-speaking-line}



\begin{quote}
Arun has already said \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{बोलतो}} in the verb lessons. In a message it needs only one new habit: a full stop that keeps it separate from the next skill.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — delayed copy}
Look at \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{बोलतो}.}, cover it, wait eight seconds, and write it. Compare the verb ending before the punctuation.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Do not join it with another verb yet.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mī vichār karto]{Keep both pieces of thinking}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M08-thinking-line}



\begin{quote}
Retrieve the known pair \textbf{\mr{विचार} \mr{करणे}}. In the sentence, \textbf{\mr{विचार}} stays beside the light verb: \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{विचार} \mr{करतो}.}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — delayed copy}
Study the line, hide it, and wait eight seconds. Write it. Check for the two verb pieces first; check the full stop second.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
One two-part verb is enough for today.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[malā marāṭhī samajte]{Return to the dative frame}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M09-understanding-line}



\begin{quote}
Compare \textbf{\mr{मला} \mr{मराठी} \mr{येते}} with \textbf{\mr{मला} \mr{मराठी} \mr{समजते}}. The frame and ending stay; only the known verb changes.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — delayed copy}
Study \textbf{\mr{मला} \mr{मराठी} \mr{समजते}.}, cover it, and wait ten seconds. Write it. Repair the dative opening first and the verb ending second.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
All six skill lines now exist separately.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dhanyavād]{One word can be a full line}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M10-thanks-line}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\mr{धन्यवाद}} from memory. It is already durable; the only message habit today is closing the one-word sentence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — delayed copy}
Look once at \textbf{\mr{धन्यवाद}.}, cover it, wait ten seconds, and write it. If the word is correct but the full stop is missing, repair only the boundary.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after the single word and its boundary.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[punhā bheṭū]{The first farewell line}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M11-again-line}



\begin{quote}
The known phrase \textbf{\mr{पुन्हा} \mr{भेटू}} promises another meeting. Keep it on a new line after thanks.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — delayed copy}
Study \textbf{\mr{पुन्हा} \mr{भेटू}.}, cover it, wait ten seconds, and write it. Compare the space between the two words before comparing the final mark.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Tomorrow's line comes in the next lesson.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[udyā bheṭū]{The dated farewell line}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M12-tomorrow-line}



\begin{quote}
Swap only the first known word: \textbf{\mr{पुन्हा} \mr{भेटू}} becomes \textbf{\mr{उद्या} \mr{भेटू}}. The message now says when the next meeting happens.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — delayed copy}
Study \textbf{\mr{उद्या} \mr{भेटू}.}, cover it, wait ten seconds, and write it. Compare \textbf{\mr{उद्या}} first; \textbf{\mr{भेटू}} was retrieved yesterday.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
All twelve lines have now been practised separately.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[opening block]{Order the opening block}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M13-opening-block}



\begin{quote}
Retrieve the three opening jobs: greet Mira, name Arun, acknowledge the meeting. Each job already has one practised line.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — controlled composition}
Put these known line cards in message order, then write them as three lines:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{\mr{भेटून} \mr{आनंद} \mr{झाला}.}
  \item \textbf{\mr{नमस्कार} \mr{मीरा}.}
  \item \textbf{\mr{माझं} \mr{नाव} \mr{अरुण} \mr{आहे}.}
\end{itemize}

Choose the order from the three jobs. Do not change any words.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop with one three-line block.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[first skills block]{Order the first three skills}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M14-skills-block-one}



\begin{quote}
Say the three jobs in English: know Marathi, read Marathi, write my name. Keep the two grammar frames separate; \textbf{\mr{मला}} and \textbf{\mr{मी}} are not interchangeable.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — controlled composition}
Choose the matching known line for each job and write the jobs in that order. Do not add a conjunction. Check the two sentence openings before spelling.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The first skills block is complete; the next three stay separate until tomorrow.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[second skills block]{Order the second three skills}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M15-skills-block-two}



\begin{quote}
Retrieve the three jobs: speak, think, understand Marathi. The middle job keeps two verb pieces; the last job returns to \textbf{\mr{मला}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — controlled composition}
Write the matching known sentence for each job in that order. Check one dimension per pass: sentence opening, then verb, then full stop.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The two skills blocks remain separate for one more lesson.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[closing block]{Order the closing block}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M16-closing-block}



\begin{quote}
Retrieve the three closing jobs: thank Mira, promise another meeting, name tomorrow. All three lines are already known.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — controlled composition}
Write one known line for each job, in that order. Keep each farewell on its own line even though both end with \textbf{\mr{भेटू}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The four message blocks are ready to meet.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[guided 32-word message]{Connect the four known blocks}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M17-guided-message}



\begin{quote}
Name the four blocks without writing: opening, first skills, second skills, closing. No block contains new Marathi.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — connected composition}
Use the four completed block lessons as cards. Put the cards in purpose order and write the message. Afterward, count words by spaces: the result has \textbf{32 words}, inside the A1 target of 30–40.

Repair in four passes: block order, sentence boundaries, verb frames, spelling. Stop after the first pass that finds a problem.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Tomorrow the cards and answer model disappear.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[independent named-reader message]{Independent 30–40-word message}

\label{lesson:MR-A1M18-independent-message}



\begin{quote}
Close every earlier lesson. On blank paper write four tiny English planning labels only: opening · skills 1 · skills 2 · closing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — connected composition, no model}
Write \textbf{30–40 words} to Mira. Introduce Arun, state the six practised Marathi skills, thank her, and close for another meeting tomorrow.

There is no romanization, line bank, block card, or visible answer model during this checkpoint. The task is untimed. When finished, count words and run one repair pass of your choice.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
This is untimed message evidence only. It does not claim form completion or the later integrated timed A1 writing task.
\end{tcolorbox}
